newsitem.title: USA: Illinois joins ranks of states suiing tobacco industry.
newsitem.headline: Illinois joins ranks of states suiing tobacco industry.

text.p: Illinois Attorney General Jim Ryan said Tuesday that he has decided to sue tobacco companies to recover state taxpayers' portion of the billions of dollars the state has paid in smoking related health care costs.

"I believe the state can prove in court that the tobacco companies engaged in misrepresentation, omission of material fact, deception and conspiracy that ultimately shortened lives and shortchanged taxpayers," Ryan said in a statement.
From 1980 to 1993, the state of Illinois incurred $2.75 billion in health care costs for services provided to Medicaid recipients attributable to smoking, according to his statement.
Fifteen other states have filed suits aimed at forcing tobacco companies to reimburse them for Medicaid costs.
